title: TVLint configuration
description: A tvlint.yaml file: `rules` say what is forbidden, `scopes` say which files each rule runs on.

rules.description: The rules, by id. The id is what violations, `scopes` and `tvl explain` refer to.

scopes.description: Entries that say which files each rule runs on. A rule that appears in no scope never runs.

aliases.description: Import prefixes that stand for a project path, like a tsconfig `paths` entry: `"@/": "src/"` turns `@/api` into `src/api`. The prefix and the path must both end with `/`, or neither.

language.description: A language a rule can apply to. Code languages are parsed; JSON, YAML and TOML are data files checked by key path.

languages.description: `python`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `rust`, `go`, `html`, `shell`, `css`, `json`, `yaml` or `toml`, or a list of them. Code languages and data languages cannot share a rule.

onlyElements.description: JSX elements (JavaScript, TypeScript) and HTML tags.

onlyObjectLiterals.description: JavaScript and TypeScript object literals, HTML attributes, and the key paths of data files.

propertyValue.description: Constraints on the value of object-literal properties (JavaScript, TypeScript) or of keys in data files (JSON, YAML, TOML).

names.description: Property name or list of names to look at. Key paths in data files.

in_call.description: Code only. Only look at objects passed directly as an argument to one of these calls, e.g. `toast.add`.

forbid_literal.description: Code only. The value must not be a string literal.

array_starts_with.description: Code only. An array-literal value must start with this element, matched as a glob on its source text, e.g. `accountID`. Other values are not checked.

forbid_value.description: Data files only. The value must not match any of these globs, e.g. `^*` or `*:latest`.

require_value.description: Data files only. The value must match one of these globs.

literalArgument.description: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust. String literals passed to calls must be listed in a data file.

calls.description: Calls whose argument is checked, as patterns like `forbid_call`.

file.description: The data file listing the allowed values, relative to the config file.

path.description: Which nodes of the file are entries, as a key path such as `errors.*`.

use.description: What an entry is called: its `key`, its `value`, or its full `path`.

report_unused.description: Also report registry entries that no call in scope uses.

forbid_raise.description: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript. Exception names that may not be raised (`throw` in JavaScript and TypeScript). Matches the full dotted name or its last part, so `HTTPException` also matches `fastapi.HTTPException`.

forbid_call.description: Call patterns that are forbidden. `*` matches anything, so `*.one` matches `session.exec(q).one()` and `console.*` matches `console.log(...)`. `new Foo()` counts as a call to `Foo`. In Rust, functions use `::`, methods use `.` (`*.unwrap`), and macros end in `!` (`println!`).

forbid_catch.description: Python only. Forbids `except` clauses that catch a class or any class inheriting from it.

subclass_of.description: Class name. Subclasses are found by name across the whole project, not by import path.

forbid_import.description: JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust. Module specifiers that may not be imported, as path globs: `*` stays within one segment, `**` crosses segments. Relative and aliased imports match by project path, anything else by the specifier as written. Rust patterns use `::` (`sqlx::**`).

except_import.description: JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust. Imports that are fine although they match `forbid_import`. Needs `forbid_import`.

forbid_element.description: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML. JSX element or HTML tag names that may not be used, e.g. `button`. JSX is matched as written, so `button` does not match `Button`; HTML tags are matched in lowercase.

forbid_property.description: JavaScript, TypeScript: object-literal property names that may not appear. JSON, YAML, TOML: key paths that must not exist, e.g. `scripts.postinstall`, `jobs.*.permissions`, `**.debug`.

within_property.description: JavaScript, TypeScript. Only count `forbid_call`, `forbid_raise` and `forbid_element` hits that sit inside an object-literal property with one of these names, e.g. `onError`.

require_property.description: JSON, YAML, TOML. Key paths that must exist, e.g. `jobs.*.timeout-minutes`: every match of the parent path must have the key.

same_keys_as.description: JSON, YAML, TOML. A file, relative to the config file, whose key paths every matched data file must have too, no more and no fewer.

same_placeholders.description: JSON, YAML, TOML. Also require the `{{placeholders}}` of each shared message to be the same as in `same_keys_as`. Needs `same_keys_as`.

max_lines.description: The most lines a file may have, in any language. A longer file is reported once, on the first line over the limit.

require_filename.description: File name globs, matched against the base name only. Every file in the rule's scope must match at least one, otherwise it is a violation reported at line 1. The only check that works without `language`.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists. Printed with every violation, so an AI agent knows the intent.

fix.description: How to comply. Printed with every violation, so an AI agent knows what to do instead.

allOf.description: property_value reads different keys in data files and in code.
Data files: needs forbid_value or require_value.
Data files do not take forbid_literal, array_starts_with or in_call.
Code: needs forbid_literal: true or array_starts_with.
Code does not take forbid_value or require_value.

rules.description: Rule ids that run on the matched files. Each must be defined under `rules`.

include.description: Glob patterns relative to the config file's directory. `*` stays within one directory, `**` crosses directories.
